attributes.scope_note: Regraded every construct-design attempt of the first six systems evaluated (450 attempts: 6 systems, 15 tasks, 5 attempts). It saw the public task text, the private reference material and the submission files, but not the reported outcome, and returned a score on the same 0 to 1 scale; agreement is measured on the binary pass outcome at 0.9. The authors state that agreement between graders does not establish independent scientific validity (Section 6.2). limitations: Two grading kinds are pooled in this one rate: deterministic-only on five tasks and deterministic multiplied by a model judge on ten. The per-task protocols keep them apart; this aggregate does not.
GPT-6 Astra is the rubric judge and is also one of the eight evaluated systems; no self-preference analysis is reported.
Table F1 records that the shipped grader result was revised for 48 of the 600 top-effort trials, so these rates embed a manual adjudication pass.

Scores come from a cloning simulator and retrospective graders, not from constructs built at the bench; the authors state the simulator cannot capture every source of variation in reagents, handling, growth or reaction outcomes (Section 6.2).
Five attempts per task over 15 tasks give wide intervals: every printed 95% interval spans at least 18 percentage points.
attributes.metric_definition: "an attempt is classified as successful when its final score is at least 0.9. The pass rate is computed by averaging the five attempt outcomes within each task and then averaging across the 15 tasks" (Section 3.4, quoted).

attributes.protocol: The agent receives the scientific objective, sequence records and supporting materials, and returns an annotated construct sequence, orderable primers where required, a construction plan and a written justification. Every task has a deterministic grader over the returned sequences, their source and the construction route. On ten of the fifteen tasks the final score is the product of the deterministic result and a GPT-6 Astra rubric score of the written reasoning and plan; on the other five it is the deterministic result alone. An attempt is classified successful at a final score of at least 0.9. Five attempts per task, each capped at two hours.

limitations: Preprint, not peer reviewed. The benchmark is published by Benchling with DNAForge, and the authors both built the benchmark and ran every system on it.

Scores come from a cloning simulator and retrospective graders, not from constructs built at the bench; the authors state the simulator cannot capture every source of variation in reagents, handling, growth or reaction outcomes (Section 6.2).

Ten of the fifteen construct-design tasks are graded in part by GPT-6 Astra as a rubric judge, which is also one of the eight evaluated systems; the authors record occasional grading inconsistency as a limitation (Section 6.2).
The simulator reports only the first blocking error, so the failure categories in Tables E1 and E2 do not establish whether later steps would have succeeded (Section 6.2).
Single-turn: the authors state the format does not reflect the multi-turn way scientists work with a model (Section 6.2).
